# Senior UI/UX Designer

## When to Use
- Evaluate or redesign user flows, screens, or interactions.
- Produce IA, wireframes, or a visual direction for a feature.
- Define or refine tokens/components, motion, accessibility, or UX copy.

## Inputs to Gather
- Goal, success metrics, and primary user task.
- Target audience, device context, and constraints.
- Existing brand or design system (if any).
- Technical constraints (platform, performance, content sources).
- Required states (empty, loading, error, edge cases).

## Procedure
1. Frame the problem
   - Restate goal, user task, and constraints.
   - Identify primary path and critical edge cases.
2. Audit the current experience (if it exists)
   - Heuristic review: clarity, feedback, control, consistency, error prevention.
   - Accessibility check: contrast, focus order, keyboard access, semantics.
3. Map the flow
   - Outline entry points, decisions, and exit paths.
   - Prioritize content by user intent (IA).
4. Draft structure
   - Create low-fi wireframes and key states.
   - Ensure one primary action per screen.
5. Define visual direction
   - Set hierarchy, type scale, spacing, and color roles.
   - If a system exists, reuse tokens; otherwise define a minimal token set.
6. Specify interaction and motion
   - Describe feedback, transitions, and micro-interactions.
   - Include reduced-motion alternatives.
7. Refine content UX
   - Improve microcopy for buttons, errors, and guidance.
8. Validate and summarize
   - Check against goals, constraints, and accessibility.
   - List risks, tradeoffs, and next steps.

## Outputs
- Flow summary (text or diagram description)
- ASCII wireframes or wireframe notes per screen/state
- UI guidance (tokens/components, layout rules)
- Interaction specs (states, motion)
- Accessibility findings and fixes
- UX copy recommendations
- Open questions and risks

## Preferred Formats
- ASCII wireframes for structure and IA

## Quality Checklist
- Clear primary action per screen
- System status is visible and timely
- Error recovery is obvious and safe
- Consistent hierarchy and spacing
- Accessible contrast and focus behavior
- Data states are covered (empty/loading/error)
- Copy is concise, action-oriented, and consistent

## Notes for Signal Lost (if applicable)
- Preserve full-viewport immersion and chapter isolation.
- Keep shell styling separate from chapter visuals.
- Favor atmospheric, narrative-driven design choices.
- Verify desktop quality; keep mobile readable.
